newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX up 0.37 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX up 0.37 pts.

text.p: Slovak major shares opened the week flat in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to shares of bank VUB pushing the SAX index up 0.55 points to 209.02.
Steel maker VSZ, once one of the bourse's most liquid shares remained mired in its current listless mood, closing unchanged at 630 crowns with only 213 traded shares.

"The situation in VSZ shares seems quite irrational to me, as the company permanently posts excellent results," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said. "I think a VSZ buying boom will break out as unexpectedly as it reversed into silence."

Bank VUB closed up 35 crowns at 1,850, while paint producer Chemolak dominated floor trading, closing down 25 crowns at 1,975 crowns. But Sykora said the majority of Chemolak shares were traded in blocks, on prices agreed outside the market.
Overall volume rose to 198,645 shares, from 145,175 shares traded on Friday, while turnover increased to 157.2 million crowns, from 155.7 million.
